scope: Theorem 4.2 (Electrical bounds for fixed tests) of the manuscript “Spectral convergence for critical FK–Ising planar maps” (preprints/Spectral-convergence-for-critical-FK-Ising-planar-maps-October-5-2026/spectral-convergence-critical-fk-ising-planar-maps.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 211 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 eeb5895c7058765f), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 22. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Consider either the primal or the dual network. Fix a countable collection of intrinsic instructions from Proposition 3.1. Suppose their activated spatial interpretations have the strict ports, confinements, and complete stars described below, compactly in an ordinary reference chart. The same assertions hold in the sphere patches covered by Proposition 3.2. In every joint representation extraction, almost surely on activation, each fixed instruction has the following properties for all sufficiently large discrete indices. (i) For the annular template (4.6), EL Am(z, r; a)  ≥ ca > 0. The constant is deterministic and depends only on the relative radii and the fixed protection margins. (ii) Fix 0 < a < b, with a protected disk buffer around B(z, br). There is a function um on the network vertices with values in [0, 1], equal to 1 at every vertex whose projected complete flag star meets B(z, ar), and equal to 0 at every vertex whose projected star meets the exterior of B(z, br). Its nonzero edge differences are supported in a fixed compact subannulus of A(z; ar, br), and E0 (um) ≤ C. The constant depends only on a, b and the chosen relative margins. In a protected patch the function is extended by the indicated constants across its two sides. (iii) Fix 0 < a < b < c. There is a probability law on simple circuits Γm in the network, compactly confined in A(z; br, cr) and surrounding B(z, ar), such that X e P(e ∈ Γm)2 ≤ Ca,b,c. A loop and a two-edge Jordan circuit are permitted simple circuits. The constant also records the fixed inner and outer collar margins. (iv) Let W be connected and open, and let P0, P1 be nonempty open subsets of W. For any fixed compact polygonal route in W from P0 to P1, there is a probability law µm of graph paths between the vertex ports, compactly confined in W, with T (µm) ≤ C < ∞. Here C may depend on the route, its clearance from Wc, and its endpoint clearances inside the ports. For translates and dilates of one fixed relative template, the constants are the same; they do not depend on the absolute radius. The eventual index belongs to the fixed activated test and may depend on it and on the sample. The assertions hold simultaneously for the chosen countable collection.
